title: Machine Learning of Quantum Entanglement from Noisy Measurements
authors: Artur Czerwinski, Maciej Wiśniewski, Paweł Moszczyński
abstract: In this work, we investigate the application of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to the identification and quantitative characterization of quantum entanglement in polarization-entangled photon pairs. The analysis is based on simulated symmetric, informationally complete, positive operator-valued measure (SIC-POVM) measurement data, where each two-qubit state is represented by a 16-dimensional measurement vector corresponding to experimentally accessible coincidence counts. The generated SIC-POVM measurement data include Poissonian shot noise. Several supervised ML algorithms, including Logistic Regression, k-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines, and Random Forests, are applied to the classification of separable and entangled states directly from raw measurement data, without explicit density matrix reconstruction or the use of conventional separability criteria. The study additionally explores clustering methods and nonlinear regression techniques for estimating continuous entanglement measures. The obtained results demonstrate that ML methods can achieve very high classification accuracy, even under extremely limited training conditions. These findings indicate that ML may provide an efficient alternative to conventional quantum-state analysis under simulated Poissonian noise conditions.
summary: The authors demonstrate that Machine Learning can effectively characterize quantum entanglement in two-qubit photon systems by analyzing raw coincidence count data from simulated measurements. By training ML models on these noisy vectors, they achieve high accuracy in distinguishing entangled states from separable ones without needing to reconstruct the full density matrix. This proposes a computationally efficient pathway for quantum state verification in experimental settings.
main_problem: The work investigates using Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to identify and quantify quantum entanglement directly from noisy measurement statistics, bypassing complex density matrix reconstruction.
main_result: ML methods achieve very high classification accuracy for distinguishing separable from entangled states, suggesting an efficient alternative to conventional state analysis under simulated noise conditions.
method: Supervised ML algorithms (e.g., Random Forests, SVMs) are trained on 16-dimensional measurement vectors derived from simulated SIC-POVM measurements of polarization-entangled photon pairs.
model_or_system: The system involves two-qubit polarization states analyzed using simulated symmetric, informationally complete POVM (SIC-POVM) measurement data. The analysis focuses on Werner states and Bell states to cover the entanglement spectrum.
key_observables: Classification of separable vs. entangled states; continuous estimation of Concurrence ($C(ho)$).
important_parameters: Poissonian shot noise level (related to total photon count $N$); entanglement parameter $p$ for Werner states.
main_assumptions: The analysis is limited to simulated data affected by Poissonian counting noise, and the performance relies on the representativeness of the training set.
paper_structure: The paper systematically applies various ML techniques (classification/regression) to datasets representing known entangled and separable states derived from simulating quantum measurements.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical challenge of characterizing fragile quantum resources like entanglement using noisy, realistic measurement data, which is crucial for experimental quantum optics and communication protocols.
